problem_markdown: Construct external triangles $ABR,BCP,CAQ$ on triangle $ABC$ so that $\angle ABR=\angle BAR=15^\circ$, $\angle CBP=\angle CAQ=45^\circ$, and $\angle BCP=\angle ACQ=30^\circ$. Prove $RQ=RP$ and $\angle QRP=90^\circ$.
solutions_markdown: Orient $ABC$ counterclockwise and construct the equilateral triangle $ABS$ externally. Put $k=1/(2\cos15^\circ)$. The sine rule gives $AQ=kAC$, $BP=kBC$, and $AR=BR=kAB$. Rotation through $45^\circ$ about $A$, followed by scaling by $k$, maps $C$ to $Q$ and $S$ to $R$. Rotation through $-45^\circ$ about $B$, with the same scale, maps $C$ to $P$ and $S$ to $R$. Thus the vectors $RQ$ and $RP$ are images of $SC$ under equal-scale rotations differing by $90^\circ$. They have equal lengths and are perpendicular.
